explanation: The characteristic roots are ±1, giving fundamental solutions e^x and e^{-x}. Their derivatives yield A=[[1,-1],[e,-e^{-1}]], so |det(A)|=e-1/e>0. Thus the homogeneous BVP has only the trivial solution. Any two inhomogeneous solutions would differ by a homogeneous solution, proving that the inhomogeneous BVP has at most one solution. Unique existence also holds here, so that stronger displayed statement is mathematically true as well.
